obligation: Bank recall request for a diverted payment
trigger: A payment (ACH or wire) is suspected to have gone to an account controlled by an attacker
deadline: Immediately on suspicion; company target 1 hour (POL-03 4.4). IC3: 'time is of the essence'
notify: The sending bank (outbound payments); for owner payments, the owner calls its own bank and the company calls its receiving bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - practical step, not a legal duty. Highest priority action in this runbook

obligation: Complaint to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: Any business email compromise with a fraudulent transfer or attempt
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount; company target same day (POL-03 4.4)
notify: IC3 (www.ic3.gov); FBI field office for losses above $1 million
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but strongly recommended; IC3 may help freeze funds

obligation: Correct SAM EFT information and alert the federal payment office (variant C)
trigger: The company's EFT (bank) information in SAM was changed without authorization, or a federal payment is missing
deadline: Immediately. If EFT information was incorrect or revised within 30 days of the Government's release of payment and the funds have left the payment office, the Government is deemed to have paid and the company must recover the funds
notify: SAM (correct the record through the Entity Administrator); Contracting Officer and paying office for each affected contract
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for all 38 federal contracts and task orders
clock_starts: Detection of the change or missing payment

obligation: Pay subcontractors on federal contracts despite a diverted payment
trigger: A payment meant for a subcontractor on a federal job went to an attacker
deadline: Subcontractor must still be paid within 7 days of the company's receipt of the Government's payment; interest penalty for late payment
notify: The subcontractor (after call-back verification of its real bank details)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for federal jobs

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (for this runbook: CUI found in a compromised mailbox, in SYS-01, or in the FPCE)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ('rapidly report'); review for evidence of compromise of covered defense information under (c)(1)(i)
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil (DoD-approved medium assurance certificate required; held by two staff)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the CUI determination (runbook 4.3) finds CUI was affected. Used on 2026-07-11 for CUI found on SYS-01 (P03 G-135)
owner: Director of Government Contracts with the Director, CMMC Program Office

obligation: Malicious software submission
trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported cyber incident
deadline: With the incident response; follow DC3 or Contracting Officer instructions; do not send malware to the Contracting Officer
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a DIBNet report is filed and malware is isolated

obligation: Preserve images and give DoD access for forensic analysis
trigger: A cyber incident reported under 252.204-7012(c)
deadline: Preserve images of affected systems and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from submission of the report; provide access and damage assessment information on DoD request
notify: DoD (on request through the Contracting Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a DIBNet report is filed

obligation: Subcontractor cyber incident report (inbound)
trigger: A subcontractor handling CUI reports a cyber incident to DoD
deadline: Subcontractor gives the DoD-assigned incident report number to the company as soon as practicable
notify: The company (Director of Government Contracts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 48 subcontractors handle CUI; flowdown required

obligation: CMMC status currency after an incident
trigger: An incident shows that a Level 1 or Level 2 requirement is no longer met in a CMMC scope
deadline: Before relying on the status for any award or making the next annual affirmation, restore compliance and re-assess; no separate incident notice duty in the clause
notify: Internal (President, Federal Group as Affirming Official); counsel; SPRS update when re-assessed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FPCE (Level 2) and enterprise FCI scope (Level 1); AQ-2 (Level 1)
clock_starts: Finding that a requirement is not met

obligation: Report discovery of covered telecommunications equipment/services during contract performance
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days
notify: Contracting Officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered by business email compromise. Listed because BTS installs video and network equipment in federal buildings (P03 G-127)

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident (including a series of related unauthorized occurrences, 17 CFR 229.106(a)) that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.5)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant. Every payment fraud event is reviewed, alone and with related occurrences

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it (for this runbook: certified payrolls with Social Security numbers, HR files, or the mailbox owner's own credentials in a compromised mailbox)
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (employees and craft workers live in at least 8 states); counsel's state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often discovery or determination of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (for example the payroll SaaS) has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Includes name with Social Security number, and an email address with the password that opens the account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; delay allowed on a written law enforcement request (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - most employees and craft workers live in Florida
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only with counsel's agreement

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - payroll, HR, and e-signature vendors that hold Florida residents' personal information

obligation: Owner notice of a compromised payment channel
trigger: Any suspicion that an owner received false remittance instructions from a company mailbox or lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to the owner's AP contact on file, then in writing
notify: Owner's AP and project representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a statutory duty

obligation: BTS client notice of exposed facility security details
trigger: The compromised mailbox or system held client building layouts, camera locations, or credentials
deadline: Per the service agreement; rotate the affected client credentials first
notify: Affected BTS clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a statutory duty

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice (social engineering sublimit)
trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy; the $2.5 million social engineering sublimit requires prompt notice and proof that verification procedures were followed
notify: Carrier breach hotline; broker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a legal duty. Use the carrier's panel counsel and forensics
owner: Vice President, Treasury with the General Counsel

obligation: Surety notice
citation: General indemnity agreements with the two sureties (contract)
trigger: A loss large enough to affect working capital or the ability to pay subcontractors on bonded work
deadline: Per the agreements
notify: Sureties
applies_at_this_tier: Check with counsel - contractual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom or extortion payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not for business email compromise (no ransom). Applies only if an extortion demand follows
